questions.q: What are the three format styles behind conditional formatting?
options: Gradient, Rules, and Field value
Bold, Italic, and Underline
Small, Medium, and Large
Import, DirectQuery, and Live Connection
questions.explain: Gradient applies a smooth color scale, Rules apply colors based on value ranges you define, and Field value pulls colors directly from a column or measure.

questions.q: What is the most common mistake when setting up rules-based conditional formatting?
options: Choosing Percent when the rule boundaries were meant as literal numbers, or vice versa
Forgetting to select a table before applying formatting
Using more than three rules at once
Applying formatting to a column header instead of a value
questions.explain: Percent bases rule boundaries on the overall min-to-max range, while Number treats them as literal values — mixing these up produces unexpected coloring.

questions.q: What do data bars show inside a table cell?
options: A proportional bar whose length scales to the cell's value
A miniature pie chart
A tooltip with the column's average
A hyperlink to another report page
questions.explain: Data bars render a bar directly in the cell — longer for higher values — letting viewers compare at a glance without a separate chart.

questions.q: Besides tables and matrices, where else does conditional formatting apply?
options: Column and bar chart colors, button slicers, cards, and several other visual types
Only in the Power BI service, never in Desktop
Nowhere else — it's exclusive to tables and matrices
Only on visuals with more than 100 rows of data
questions.explain: Conditional formatting extends well beyond tables — it's available on many visual types, using the same Gradient, Rules, and Field value styles.

questions.q: What's the advantage of coloring by a calculated measure (Field value) over building several rules by hand?
options: It keeps the coloring logic visible and testable as a formula, which is often faster to maintain once the logic gets complex
It's the only method that works on numeric columns
It automatically updates without any user action, unlike rules
Rules-based formatting cannot be combined with Field value in the same report
questions.explain: Writing a measure that returns a hex or named color directly (via SWITCH or IF) keeps complex coloring logic in one testable formula instead of scattered across dialog rules.
